title: Nan Madol
summary: Nan Madol is a ceremonial and royal centre of more than 100 artificial islets off the south-east coast of Pohnpei, in Micronesia. Chiefs of the Saudeleur dynasty had its palaces, temples and tombs enclosed by walls of columnar basalt and coral, with tomb walls up to about 8 m high, mostly raised between 1200 and 1500 CE.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO says the structures were built between 1200 and 1500 CE; the US National Park Service nomination dates megalithic building at Usendau to about AD 800 and occupation from at least AD 400. The start is UNESCO's, with a wide minus range for those earlier dates. End is the present: the ruins stand.

footprint.description: An island-like rectangular platform, the 50 by 60 m Nan Dauas islet, enclosed by basalt-prism walls laid header-and-stretcher over a boulder foundation, with a central tomb inside the outer walls. The wider complex has over 90 artificial islets up to about 115 by 100 m (NPS).

phases.description: UNESCO dates the stone palaces, temples, tombs and residential domains to 1200-1500 CE, the Saudeleur period; the evaluation gives megalithic construction between 1200-1300 and 1500-1600 CE.
UNESCO calls the remains ruins. The sources opened give no date for abandonment or collapse; the start year is the end of the stated building span.

reviewer_note: Shape block (the walled Nandauwas islet; the complex as a whole is a group of islets). Heights conflict: NPS gives 8.1 m maximum, the UNESCO evaluation 6-7 m; the model takes NPS's. Least sure of the start date (earlier radiocarbon dates exist) and of the 'ruined' phase start, which is bridged.
